# Network and permissions

<!-- Generated by `npm run docs:network` from packages/scanner/src/scanner-surface.ts and init/access-guide.ts. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every request scanent can make, and every permission it asks for. This page is rendered from
the surface the scanner declares in its own code, the same declaration whose hash is in every
signed report, so it lists what the code can do and nothing else.

Scanner `inflect-agent-harness-scanner`, version 0.15.0. One image holds 2 scanners, and this page lists the requests of all of them:

- The agent scanner: report contract `inflect-agent-harness/4`, written as `report.signed.json`; source kinds `entra-sp`, `okta-app`, `vault`, `mcp`, `runtime`, `cicd`, `inflect-register`, `code`, `gcp-sa`.
- The integrations scanner: report contract `scanent-integrations/1`, written as `report.integrations.signed.json`; source kinds `entra-integrations`, `okta-integrations`, `github-integrations`.

A run reads only the sources its configuration names, and writes one signed report for each scanner
whose sources it names, all with the same key and the same scan id.

Manifest hash: `sha256:885886a3315b34fb8bc870a37fcd34993ee77af4abdaf9fca5052311b8f1f053`

The hash is SHA-256 over the canonical JSON of the declared surface, every scanner's requests in one.
A scanner that can reach anything this page does not list has a different hash, and every report it
signs, of either contract, carries it.

## What holds for every request

- **https only**, to port 443. A URL with a user name or password in it is refused.
- **Redirects are refused.** A redirect ends the read; it is never followed, because the request carries a credential.
- **A link to another host or another path is not followed.** A next-page link is used only when it stays on the origin and the path of the listing being read.
- **Bounded.** At most 4 MiB per response and 64 MiB per source, and one deadline per source (`timeBoxSeconds`). Past a bound the source is reported as not read in full.
- **No retry.** A request that fails is not sent again in the same scan.
- **Only GET**, except the requests listed under "Token exchanges", "MCP servers", "The register read" and "The one post" below.
- **No other outbound traffic.** The scanner sends no telemetry and checks for no update. Besides the requests on this page it makes DNS lookups for the hosts it reaches.

To list the hosts one configuration reaches, run `scanent hosts --config <file>`.

## Hosts and grants at a glance

| Scanner | Source | Read from | Token from | Grant |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| agents | `entra-sp` | `graph.microsoft.com` (fixed) | `login.microsoftonline.com` | Microsoft Graph application permission Application.Read.All, with admin consent |
| agents | `vault` | each vault you configure, which must be on `*.vault.azure.net` | `login.microsoftonline.com` | Key Vault Reader on each listed vault (RBAC vaults). For a vault on access policies: List on secrets and List on certificates, and nothing else |
| agents | `okta-app` | the Okta org you configure, which must be on `*.okta.com` or `*.oktapreview.com` | none | An SSWS API token created by a user holding the Read-only Administrator role only |
| agents | `cicd` | `api.github.com` (fixed) | none | A fine-grained personal access token (or a GitHub App installation) limited to the listed repositories, with Contents: Read-only and Secrets: Read-only. Metadata: Read-only is added by GitHub |
| agents | `gcp-sa` | `iam.googleapis.com` (fixed) | `oauth2.googleapis.com` | roles/iam.serviceAccountViewer on each listed project, held by a dedicated service account; one JSON key for that account |
| agents | `runtime` | `api.smith.langchain.com` or `eu.api.smith.langchain.com` (fixed, by the region you configure), or the self-hosted host you configure | none | A service key holding the workspace Viewer role |
| agents | `mcp` | each MCP server you configure | none | Per server, a token that can list tools and nothing else; none when the server takes none |
| agents | `code` | none | none | Read access to the listed directories for the user the scanner runs as |
| agents | `inflect-register` | the tenant you configure | the same tenant | An API key bound to the scanner agent with the admin:harness_ingest scope, plus mcp:read when the register is read |
| integrations | `entra-integrations` | `graph.microsoft.com` (fixed) | `login.microsoftonline.com` | Microsoft Graph application permissions Application.Read.All and Directory.Read.All, with admin consent; AuditLog.Read.All as well only when readSignInActivity is set |
| integrations | `okta-integrations` | the Okta org you configure, which must be on `*.okta.com` or `*.oktapreview.com` | none | An SSWS API token created by a user holding the Read-only Administrator role only. It may be the token the okta-app source uses |
| integrations | `github-integrations` | `api.github.com` (fixed) | none | A fine-grained personal access token whose resource owner is the organisation, with the organisation permissions Administration: Read-only and Webhooks: Read-only, created by an organisation owner |

## The agent scanner

Report contract `inflect-agent-harness/4`. The requests of its sources:

### Microsoft Entra ID (service principals and app registrations)

Source kind `entra-sp`. Reads from: `graph.microsoft.com` (fixed).

| Method | Path | What is kept |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `/v1.0/applications` | App registrations: ids, the ids and dates of their password and key credentials, and the ids of their owners. Selected by name; no secret text, hint or display name is kept |
| GET | `/v1.0/servicePrincipals` | Service principals: ids, type, whether enabled, the owning directory, credential ids and dates, and owner ids |

Before reading, one token exchange: `POST https://login.microsoftonline.com/{directoryId}/oauth2/v2.0/token`. See "Token exchanges".

**Grant asked for.** Microsoft Graph application permission Application.Read.All, with admin consent.

**Must not be granted.**

- Any ReadWrite permission
- Directory.* permissions, unless the same application also reads for `entra-integrations`, which needs Directory.Read.All
- Any delegated permission
- Any directory role

**Never requested.** The API offers these, and the scanner cannot make them:

- `POST /v1.0/applications/{id}/addPassword`: creates a client secret.
- `PATCH /v1.0/servicePrincipals/{id}`: changes a service principal.
- `GET /v1.0/users`: the directory of people is not read; an owner is kept as an id only.

### Azure Key Vault (credential metadata)

Source kind `vault`. Reads from: each vault you configure, which must be on `*.vault.azure.net`.

| Method | Path | What is kept |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `/secrets` | Secret metadata: name, whether enabled, created and expiry dates, tags. The listing carries no value |
| GET | `/certificates` | Certificate metadata: name, whether enabled, dates, tags |

Before reading, one token exchange: `POST https://login.microsoftonline.com/{directoryTenantId}/oauth2/v2.0/token`. See "Token exchanges".

**Grant asked for.** Key Vault Reader on each listed vault (RBAC vaults). For a vault on access policies: List on secrets and List on certificates, and nothing else.

**Must not be granted.**

- Key Vault Secrets User
- Key Vault Administrator
- Get on secrets: each of these reads or changes secret values

**Never requested.** The API offers these, and the scanner cannot make them:

- `GET /secrets/{name}`: returns the secret value.
- `GET /secrets/{name}/{version}`: returns the secret value.
- `GET /keys`: keys are not read.

### Okta (service apps and API tokens)

Source kind `okta-app`. Reads from: the Okta org you configure, which must be on `*.okta.com` or `*.oktapreview.com`.

| Method | Path | What is kept |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/v1/apps` | OIDC applications: id, sign-on mode, application type, and the owner written in the profile |
| GET | `/api/v1/api-tokens` | API token metadata: id, the user it belongs to, created and expiry dates. Never a token value, which Okta does not return |
| GET | `/api/v1/api-tokens/current` | The id of the token the scanner itself reads with, so its own token is not reported as somebody's |

**Grant asked for.** An SSWS API token created by a user holding the Read-only Administrator role only.

**Must not be granted.**

- Super Administrator
- Org Administrator
- App Administrator
- API Access Management Administrator

**Never requested.** The API offers these, and the scanner cannot make them:

- `GET /api/v1/apps/{id}/credentials/secrets`: returns client secrets.
- `GET /api/v1/users`: the directory of people is not read.
- `DELETE /api/v1/api-tokens/{id}`: revokes a token.

### GitHub Actions (workflows and secret names)

Source kind `cicd`. Reads from: `api.github.com` (fixed).

| Method | Path | What is kept |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `/repos/{owner}/{repo}` | The repository's default branch |
| GET | `/repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/.github/workflows` | The names of the workflow files on the default branch |
| GET | `/repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/.github/workflows/{file}` | One workflow file, read as text for its permissions and the secret names it refers to |
| GET | `/repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/secrets` | The names and update dates of Actions secrets. GitHub returns no value here |

**Grant asked for.** A fine-grained personal access token (or a GitHub App installation) limited to the listed repositories, with Contents: Read-only and Secrets: Read-only. Metadata: Read-only is added by GitHub.

**Must not be granted.**

- Any Read and write permission
- Actions
- Administration
- Workflows
- A classic token with the repo scope

**Never requested.** The API offers these, and the scanner cannot make them:

- `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/secrets/{name}`: one secret is never asked for by name.
- `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/{path}`: no file outside `.github/workflows` is read.
- `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runs`: runs and their logs are not read.

### Google Cloud (service accounts and their keys)

Source kind `gcp-sa`. Reads from: `iam.googleapis.com` (fixed).

| Method | Path | What is kept |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `/v1/projects/{project}/serviceAccounts` | Service accounts: unique id, e-mail address (to tell account types apart, not reported), whether disabled |
| GET | `/v1/projects/{project}/serviceAccounts/{account}/keys` | User-managed key metadata: key id and validity dates. Google returns no key material here |

Before reading, one token exchange: `POST https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token`. See "Token exchanges".

**Grant asked for.** roles/iam.serviceAccountViewer on each listed project, held by a dedicated service account; one JSON key for that account.

**Must not be granted.**

- roles/iam.serviceAccountAdmin
- roles/iam.serviceAccountKeyAdmin
- roles/iam.serviceAccountUser
- roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator
- Editor
- Owner

**Never requested.** The API offers these, and the scanner cannot make them:

- `POST /v1/projects/{project}/serviceAccounts/{account}/keys`: creates a key and returns its private half.
- `POST /v1/projects/{project}/serviceAccounts/{account}:getIamPolicy`: policies are not read.
- `POST /v1/projects/{project}/serviceAccounts/{account}:signBlob`: acts as the account.

### LangSmith (tracing projects and deployments)

Source kind `runtime`. Reads from: `api.smith.langchain.com` or `eu.api.smith.langchain.com` (fixed, by the region you configure), or the self-hosted host you configure.

| Method | Path | What is kept |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/v1/sessions` | Tracing projects: id, start time, and aggregate counts of tool runs by tool name over the configured window. No run, input or output |
| GET | `/v2/deployments` | Deployments: id and the tracing project each writes to. Only when `readDeployments` is set, because the listing also carries deployment secrets, which are dropped with the page |
| GET | `/api-host/v2/deployments` | The same deployments listing, on a self-hosted LangSmith |

**Grant asked for.** A service key holding the workspace Viewer role.

**Must not be granted.**

- The Editor or Admin role
- A personal access token of an administrator

**Never requested.** The API offers these, and the scanner cannot make them:

- `GET /api/v1/runs/{id}`: returns a run with its inputs and outputs.
- `POST /api/v1/runs/query`: returns runs with their inputs and outputs.
- `GET /api/v1/datasets`: datasets are not read.

### MCP servers (tool listings)

Source kind `mcp`. Reads from: each MCP server you configure.

To each server the scanner sends `POST` requests carrying these JSON-RPC messages, and no other:

- `initialize`
- `notifications/initialized`
- `tools/list`

It keeps each tool's name and annotations, and a hash of the whole listing. It offers the server no capability (no sampling, no roots, no elicitation).

**Grant asked for.** Per server, a token that can list tools and nothing else; none when the server takes none.

**Must not be granted.**

- Any scope that lets the token call a tool

**Never sent.** `tools/call`, `resources/list`, `resources/read`, `prompts/list`, `prompts/get`, or any other message: no tool is ever called on an estate's server.

An MCP server is a host the estate names, so before each request its name is resolved and every
address checked: loopback, link-local (cloud metadata) and unspecified addresses are always
refused, and a private address is refused unless the configuration lists its range. The same
holds for a self-hosted LangSmith.

### Agent code (local directories)

Source kind `code`. No network request at all.

- File operations: `lstat`, `readdir`, `readFile`. Nothing is written, created, renamed or removed.
- Files read: those ending `.py`, `.js`, `.mjs`, `.cjs`, `.jsx`, `.ts`, `.mts`, `.cts`, `.tsx`.
- Directories not entered: `node_modules`, `.git`, `.hg`, `.svn`, `__pycache__`, `.venv`, `venv`, `site-packages`, `.tox`, `.mypy_cache`, `.pytest_cache`, `.ruff_cache`, `.next`, `dist`, `build`, `coverage`.
- Symbolic links followed: never. Code executed: never. Files are parsed as text.
- Bounds: 1 MiB per file that is parsed, 20,000 files, 128 MiB in total. A larger file, up to 16 MiB, is read only to look for the name of a framework or of a model provider's SDK and is never parsed; one that names one is reported as not read.

**Grant asked for.** Read access to the listed directories for the user the scanner runs as.

**Must not be granted.**

- Write access: mount the roots read-only

### The register read

Source kind `inflect-register`. Reads from: the tenant you configure, and only when this source is configured.

1. `POST /api/mcp/token`: the ingest key is exchanged for a short-lived token whose audience is `get_harness_register` and nothing else.
2. `POST /api/mcp` carrying `initialize`, `notifications/initialized`, `tools/call`. The one tool called is `get_harness_register`, with no arguments.

**Grant asked for.** An API key bound to the scanner agent with the admin:harness_ingest scope, plus mcp:read when the register is read.

**Must not be granted.**

- Any other scope

**Never sent.** A call of any other tool, or an exchange for any other audience.

## The integrations scanner

Report contract `scanent-integrations/1`. The requests of its sources:

### Microsoft Entra ID (applications and what they were granted)

Source kind `entra-integrations`. Reads from: `graph.microsoft.com` (fixed).

| Method | Path | What is kept |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `/v1.0/servicePrincipals` | Service principals: ids, application id, type, whether enabled, the owning directory, the verified publisher's id, each app role's id and value, credential ids and dates, and owner ids. A display name is kept only when it is printable and not secret-shaped; no description, hint or secret text is kept |
| GET | `/v1.0/applications` | This directory's own app registrations: the application id and the ids of their owners, to add to the owners of each one's service principal. Nothing else is kept |
| GET | `/v1.0/oauth2PermissionGrants` | Delegated grants: the application, the API, the consent type and the scopes. For a grant made for named people the people are counted, and their ids are dropped |
| GET | `/v1.0/servicePrincipals/{id}/appRoleAssignments` | One application's application permissions: the app role's id and the API it is on. No display name is kept |
| GET | `/beta/reports/servicePrincipalSignInActivities` | Each application's last sign-in, kept to the day. Only when `readSignInActivity` is set; a beta report of Microsoft Graph |

Before reading, one token exchange: `POST https://login.microsoftonline.com/{directoryId}/oauth2/v2.0/token`. See "Token exchanges".

**Grant asked for.** Microsoft Graph application permissions Application.Read.All and Directory.Read.All, with admin consent; AuditLog.Read.All as well only when readSignInActivity is set.

**Must not be granted.**

- Any ReadWrite permission
- Any delegated permission
- Any directory role
- AuditLog.Read.All, unless readSignInActivity is set

**Never requested.** The API offers these, and the scanner cannot make them:

- `DELETE /v1.0/oauth2PermissionGrants/{id}`: revokes a delegated grant.
- `DELETE /v1.0/servicePrincipals/{id}/appRoleAssignments/{assignment}`: removes an application permission.
- `GET /v1.0/users/{id}`: the person who consented is not read; a grant made for named people is a count.
- `GET /v1.0/auditLogs/signIns`: sign-in records of people are not read; only each application's own last sign-in is.

### Okta (applications and the Okta API scopes granted to them)

Source kind `okta-integrations`. Reads from: the Okta org you configure, which must be on `*.okta.com` or `*.oktapreview.com`.

| Method | Path | What is kept |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/v1/apps` | Every application of the org: id, the definition's name key (to leave out Okta's own Admin Console, End-User Dashboard and Browser Plugin, which are counted and not reported), label (kept only when printable and not secret-shaped), status and sign-on mode. No credentials, settings or profile are kept |
| GET | `/api/v1/apps/{app}/grants` | One application's consent grants: the Okta API scope of each, and whether it is active. Who consented (`userId`), the client id and the issuer are dropped |

**Grant asked for.** An SSWS API token created by a user holding the Read-only Administrator role only. It may be the token the okta-app source uses.

**Must not be granted.**

- Super Administrator
- Org Administrator
- App Administrator
- API Access Management Administrator

**Never requested.** The API offers these, and the scanner cannot make them:

- `GET /api/v1/apps/{app}/credentials/secrets`: returns client secrets.
- `DELETE /api/v1/apps/{app}/grants/{grant}`: revokes a grant.
- `GET /api/v1/logs`: the System Log is not read; it is where Okta keeps an application's use, which is why "unused" is not concluded for Okta.
- `GET /api/v1/users/{user}`: the person who consented is not read.

### GitHub (an organisation's app installations and webhooks)

Source kind `github-integrations`. Reads from: `api.github.com` (fixed).

| Method | Path | What is kept |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `/orgs/{org}/installations` | The organisation's GitHub App installations: installation and app ids, the app's slug, its permissions and their levels, its repository selection, its events and whether it is suspended |
| GET | `/orgs/{org}/hooks` | The organisation's webhooks: id, events, whether active, the creation date, and the target's HOST. The URL is reduced to its host where it is read; its path, its query and the hook's secret are never kept, logged or reported |

**Grant asked for.** A fine-grained personal access token whose resource owner is the organisation, with the organisation permissions Administration: Read-only and Webhooks: Read-only, created by an organisation owner.

**Must not be granted.**

- Any Read and write permission
- Any repository permission
- Members, or any organisation permission other than the two above
- A classic token: listing webhooks takes admin:org_hook, which can also change them

**Never requested.** The API offers these, and the scanner cannot make them:

- `GET /orgs/{org}/hooks/{hook}/config`: returns a webhook's configuration, its URL included.
- `GET /orgs/{org}/hooks/{hook}/deliveries`: returns what was sent to a webhook.
- `DELETE /orgs/{org}/installations/{installation}`: uninstalls an app.
- `GET /orgs/{org}/audit-log`: the audit log is not read; it is where an installation's use is, which is why "unused" is not concluded for GitHub.

## Token exchanges

A token exchange is a POST by protocol. It asks the identity provider for a token to read with,
and changes nothing in the estate. The token is held in memory for one source read and is never
written or logged.

| For | Request | Grant type |
|---|---|---|
| `azure-key-vault` | `POST https://login.microsoftonline.com/{directoryTenantId}/oauth2/v2.0/token` | client credentials |
| `entra` | `POST https://login.microsoftonline.com/{directoryId}/oauth2/v2.0/token` | client credentials |
| `gcp-iam` | `POST https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token` | JWT bearer (RFC 7523): an assertion signed with the service-account key |
| `entra-integrations` | `POST https://login.microsoftonline.com/{directoryId}/oauth2/v2.0/token` | client credentials |

## The one post

Only when the `inflect` output is in effect, the agent scanner's signed report is sent to the tenant you configure:

- `POST /api/t/{tenantSlug}/admin/agents/harness-scans`

The body is the signed report, byte for byte what the file output writes as `report.signed.json`.
The integrations scanner's report (`report.integrations.signed.json`) is not posted anywhere: the tenant has no ingest for it yet, and the scanner says so in its log.
With no `inflect` output (`--out`, `--dry-run`, or a configuration that names no tenant) nothing is posted anywhere.

## The egress proof

Only when the configuration has an `egress` block. Before reading, the scanner checks that it is
confined to its proxy. Each connection is opened and closed; nothing is sent through a tunnel.

| Request | Through | Target | Expected |
|---|---|---|---|
| CONNECT | configured proxy | `{inflectHost}:443` | 200 |
| CONNECT | configured proxy | `{canaryHost}:443` | 403 |
| TCP | direct | `{inflectHost}:443` | refused |

## Declared, and not reachable from a configuration

The surface also declares 5 read calls on one gRPC service, `openshell.v1.OpenShell` (`ListSandboxes`, `GetSandbox`, `GetSandboxPolicyStatus`, `ListSandboxProviders`, `GetProviderProfile`), under the scopes `sandbox:read` and `provider:read`.
This version carries no gRPC transport and no configuration can select that source: a scan makes no such call.
It is listed because it is part of the manifest hash.

## How this page is held to the code

- It is rendered from the declared surface; a test fails when the committed file differs from the rendering.
- A test runs every source and every preflight against a recorder and fails on any request that is not on the surface, and on any declared request that nothing makes.
- The interface a source is given has one verb, `getJson`, and no method parameter, so a source has no way to spell a write.
